packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader)

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author before or during this reading.
Beyond the stated rules I did one thing: I listed the file names of the packet directory itself (to learn how many image files there were). That listing showed the name "packet.json"; I did not open it. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001.jpg to image-009.jpg. No web, search, catalogue or edition was used.

OVERALL CONFIDENCE: LOW. The hand is a very rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive with many suspension loops; the surface is stained and speckled. Most of what follows is tentative. I could secure recurring words and some phrases, not continuous sentences. Please treat every line as a proposal to be checked, not as a transcription of record.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- image-001.jpg is a reduced overview of one face; image-002 to image-009 are overlapping native-resolution tiles of that same face, arranged two across and four down (002 top-left, 003 top-right, 004/005 upper middle, 006/007 lower middle, 008/009 bottom). Only one face is supplied.
- Upright orientation. A scale bar at the foot of the overview shows the leaf is roughly 11 units wide (units look like centimetres) - a small leaf or slip. Edges are torn and wormed; a long diagonal cut/tear crosses the lower left; several holes at the right edge.
- Single main text block, long lines, about 30 lines in an upper block and about 20 in a lower block. The two blocks are separated by a blank band about three lines deep (roughly 58-62% of the way down). The last line of the upper block is short (ends mid-line), so the blank band looks like a paragraph/section break.
- A vertical ruled or scored line runs down the left side. To the LEFT of it there is a narrow strip of writing (a few letters to one word per line) running the whole height. Observation only: I cannot tell from the images whether this is a column of marginal notes, or the line-ends of a neighbouring column/page that continues beyond the leaf edge. Tentative interpretation: line-ends of adjacent text, since the strip lines sit at the same pitch as the main lines.
- No running title, no rubric, no coloured ink, no enlarged or decorated initials are visible. No interlinear gloss that I can separate from the main lines.
- Underlining: several stretches are underlined in the text ink - one in the upper block (visible in image-003 line 11 / image-004 line 1 / image-005 line 2) and several consecutive lines in the lower block (image-006 lines 9-13, image-007 lines 8-13, image-008/009 upper lines). Tentative interpretation: underlined quoted text or lemmata with discussion around them; I could not confirm this by reading.
- A paragraph-type mark appears possible in image-003 line 6 before what I read tentatively as "p(ri)ma ꝯclusio".

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: (a) top of the upper block (image-002, image-003); (b) end of the upper block and start of the lower block around the blank band (image-006, image-007), which is the clearest area; (c) some lines at the foot (image-009).
Left essentially unread: the left marginal strip; most of image-004 and image-005 (middle of the upper block); most of image-008 (lower left, stained and cut).

3. RECURRING WORDS I AM FAIRLY CONFIDENT OF
- "ꝯſiderabilis / ꝯſiderabilia / ꝯſiderabili" (considerabil-), many times, especially at the end of the upper block.
- "ꝯſiderat(ur)" / "ꝯſideratio(n)e".
- "p(ri)mo modo" (twice, image-006 lines 6 and 7).
- "aggregat-" (aggregatio / aggregato / aggregatiue), several times in the lower block.
- "pluribus" (image-007).
- "nō" (non), "ſ(ed)", "et", the 2-shaped sign for "est" or "et".

4. TENTATIVE LINE READINGS
Conventions: ( ) proposed expansion; (?) after a word = uncertain reading; [illegible] = I could not read it; ꝯ = the con-/com- sign; "2" = a 2-shaped sign which I take to be "est" in most places.

4e. image-009.jpg (bottom right)
line 1: aggregato(?) [illegible; same line as image-007 line 14]

line 8: [illegible] vnitas(?) [illegible] ut h(?)[..] [illegible]
lines 9-15: not read; "v(er)o", "de", "pluribus(?)" appear to recur. The last two lines are cropped by the lower edge of the leaf and by damage at the right corner.

4f. Left strip (image-002, 004, 006, 008): not read. Isolated shapes only, e.g. image-002 strip lines 1-3 "[..] vbi(?)", "[..]orbat(?)", "erat(?) in".

5. LIMITATIONS
- This is a low-confidence reading. I could not produce a ten-line connected span on this face; the hand defeated me, not (for the most part) the leaf. The areas around the blank band (image-006/007) are physically legible and should yield more to a reader familiar with this type of cursive.
- Damage: stains over the lower third; diagonal cut and losses lower left (image-008); holes along the right edge clip some line-ends (image-005, image-007, image-009); top-left corner torn away, so the first main lines start short.
- The relationship of the left strip to the main block is undetermined; a wider view that includes whatever lay to the left would settle it.
- Because the same lines run across paired tiles, line numbers of paired tiles (002/003, 004/005, 006/007, 008/009) refer to the same physical lines where the numbers coincide only approximately; the tiles also overlap vertically (e.g. image-002 lines 10-15 reappear at the top of image-004). Repeated lines are not additional text.
- Subject matter, as far as the secure words go: repeated talk of what is "considerabile", "primo modo", and of "aggregat-" and "pluribus". I draw no inference about work or author.
